sanskrit: evamuktastu luṃpo'sau hyājagāma tvarānvitaḥ | mahākālavanaṃ ramyaṃ maharṣigaṇasevitam || 28 || prāptaḥ svargopamaṃ bhūpaḥ śiprayā pariśobhitam | viveśa ca mudā yukto dṛṣṭvā liṃgamanuttamam || 29 || snātvā śiprājale puṇye mahāpātakanāśane | darśanāttasya liṃgasya divyarūpo vabhūva ha || 30 ||
english: On being told thus, Luṃpa hastened to this place, the beautiful Mahākālavana resorted to by multitudes of great sages. The king reached the place comparable to Svarga and rendered splendid by Śiprā. He entered the precincts and saw the excellent Liṅga. He took his bath in the holy water of Śiprā, destructive of great sins. By seeing the Liṅga, he assumed a divine form. Rid of the disease of leprosy and liberated from the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, the king became blessed, O Pārvatī, by seeing (the Liṅga) alone. The king spent that night there along with the wife and honoured the sages very much.
